subject: forensic-medicine
title: Decomposition and late postmortem changes

steps.tx: **Putrefaction** is the breakdown of soft tissue after death, driven largely by **gut bacteria** that spread through the body once the bowel wall loses its integrity. Anaerobic organisms such as **Clostridium welchii** generate gas and foul-smelling products. Because it begins hours to days after death, putrefaction is a **late postmortem change** and cannot be used to confirm death early on.
steps.say: Putrefaction is the breakdown of soft tissue after death, driven largely by gut bacteria that spread through the body once the bowel wall loses its integrity. Anaerobic organisms such as Clostridium welchii release gas and foul-smelling products. Because it starts hours to days after death, putrefaction is a late postmortem change, so it cannot be relied on to confirm death early on.

steps.tx: The **liver** turns spongy, showing a honeycomb or Swiss cheese look from gas bubbles, later turning coal black. Putrefaction is **retarded** by carbolic acid, arsenic, zinc chloride and strychnine, and is facilitated by air, moisture and temperatures between 10 and 45 degrees Celsius.
steps.say: The liver turns spongy, showing a honeycomb or Swiss cheese look from gas bubbles, and later turns coal black. Putrefaction is retarded by carbolic acid, arsenic, zinc chloride and strychnine. It is facilitated by air, moisture and temperatures between 10 and 45 degrees Celsius.

steps.tx: **Adipocere** is saponification of fat, forming a waxy soap in wet, warm conditions. **Mummification** is drying of the body in hot, dry air, preserving features and leaving the body nearly odourless. Maceration is aseptic autolysis of a dead fetus in liquor amnii.
steps.say: Adipocere is saponification of fat, forming a waxy soap in wet, warm conditions. Mummification is drying of the body in hot, dry air, preserving features and leaving the body nearly odourless. Maceration is aseptic autolysis of a dead fetus in liquor amnii.

steps.tx: Flies lay eggs within 6 to 12 hours, and **maggots** appear about 2 to 3 days after death, so they help estimate the time since death. Last to putrefy among soft tissues are the **uterus** in women and the **prostate** in men, and overall bone is last. Bone remains are seen in 1 to 5 years when exposed.
steps.say: Flies lay eggs within 6 to 12 hours, and maggots appear about 2 to 3 days after death, so they help estimate the time since death. The uterus in women and the prostate in men are the last soft tissues to putrefy, and overall bone is last. Exposed bone remains in 1 to 5 years.
